documentation: Use triple-double-quoted docstrings for public modules, classes and functions, and non-obvious private functions.
Start with a concise summary; add Args, Returns or Yields, and Raises sections when applicable.
Describe semantics and constraints rather than repeating type annotations; document public attributes where useful.
Test docstrings are optional when test names already explain intent; explain unusual fixtures or dependencies.
rules: Group standard-library, third-party and local imports; avoid wildcard imports.
Annotate public interfaces and complex data structures; allow clear local inference.
Avoid mutable default arguments and implicit shared mutable state.
Catch specific exceptions; broad catches need deliberate boundary handling or re-raising.
Use context managers for resources and explicit boundary validation rather than assertions for user input.
